title: Senior Employability: Meaningful Employment and its Value for Businesses and Singapore
what_it_is: Senior Employability: Meaningful Employment and its Value for Businesses and Singapore

sections.label: Singapore population ageing statistics
sections.summary: By 2030 one in four Singaporeans will be 65 and above, and Singapore will rank among the top 10 aged countries in 2050.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: By 2030, one in four Singaporeans will be aged 65 and above.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Based on the United Nations' report on the world's population ageing in 2019, Singapore will be amongst the top 10 aged countries in the world in 2050 and the second highest country with the largest percentage point increase in the share of older persons in the world.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Life expectancy, as we all discussed earlier, of Singaporeans is going up, and in 2020, it is 83.93 years with healthy life expectancy at 73.7 years for males and 75.2 years for females.

sections.label: Seniors survey respondents
sections.summary: Nine hundred and thirty-four seniors of diverse profiles responded to the survey.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Nine hundred and thirty-four seniors of diverse profiles responded to the survey.

sections.label: OECD older worker hiring rates
sections.summary: An OECD 2020 report stated the hiring rate for older workers aged 55 to 64 is half that for younger workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: In the OECD report on Promoting an Age-Inclusive Workforce 2020, it was reported that across OECD, the hiring rate for older workers aged 55 to 64 is half that for younger workers, and the challenges in recruitment posed barriers for older workers.

sections.label: Younger workers survey paradox
sections.summary: The survey found 94% of younger workers acknowledged advantages of working with older colleagues while 78% faced challenges.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: From the survey with younger workers, the findings showed a paradox, where a high proportion of respondents, which is 94%, which caught me by surprise as well, acknowledged the advantages of working with older colleagues and yet, a relatively high number of respondents, 78%, faced challenges working with older colleagues.

sections.label: Recommendations on learning and workforce
sections.summary: The recommendations cover structural change in learning and work organisation, and better support for a multi-generational workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: My recommendations touch on two areas: one, structural change required in how we learn and organise work; two, the need to better support a multi-generational workforce.

sections.label: Structural change for senior employment
sections.summary: Structural change is needed in learning, employment models, work processes, HR practices and career planning to enable seniors' meaningful employment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Minister Ong Ye Kung touched on this point about life stages determining the different points in terms of health and I think we need to also look at it in terms of work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: We need structural change to policies around learning, employment models, work processes, HR practices, career planning to enable seniors to have more meaningful employment and for employers and Singapore to effectively tap the potential of this segment and growing pool of talent.

sections.label: Multi-generational workforce study findings
sections.summary: A WEF, AARP and OECD study found investing in a multi-generational workforce raises GDP per capita by almost 19% over three decades, with productivity and retention benefits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: A World Economic Forum, AARP and the OECD study found that investing in a multi-generational workforce actually increases GDP per capita by almost 19% in three decades.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The key learnings that were released by OECD revealed that the multi-generational workforces increased productivity, leads to better retention of experiences and know-how, increases resilience and better access to multi-skilled teams and other benefits.

sections.label: Singapore multi-generational workforce reforms
sections.summary: The speaker urges MOM to support reforms for a multi-generational workforce, citing the Forward Singapore Movement as a platform for stakeholders to chart senior employment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: We must do more in Singapore to understand and provide the environment to harness the strength of a multi-generational workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I do hope that MOM will agree with me on the benefits of a multi-generational workforce and will help put in place the right reforms in our system to make meaningful policies that will support this environment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I want to say that the Forward Singapore Movement provides an opportunity and an important platform for all stakeholders young and old, individuals, employers, Government, unions, educational and training institutions, trade associations and industry bodies to come together to chart the way forward for meaningful employment of seniors.

sections.label: Employment rates for older workers
sections.summary: From 2019 to 2021, employment rose from 67.6% to 69% for ages 55 to 64 and from 41.7% to 49.0% for ages 65 to 69.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: From 2019 to 2021, the employment rate for those aged 55 to 64 increased from 67.6% to 69% while those aged 65 to 69 increased from 41.7% to 49.0%.

sections.label: Retirement and re-employment age increases
sections.summary: With tripartite partners, retirement and re-employment ages were raised to 63 and 68 from 1 July this year, targeting 65 and 70 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Together with our tripartite partners, we have put in place a roadmap to support that.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We have raised the retirement and re-employment age to 63 and 68 respectively from 1 July this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Our goal is to increase it to 65 and 70 respectively by 2030.

sections.label: Skills upgrading and reskilling support
sections.summary: A skills upgrading ecosystem supports career switches through the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package and Career Transition Programme, with up to 90% salary and training support via reskilling programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We have put in place a skills upgrading ecosystem to support career switches through the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package and, more recently, SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: We also provide enhanced salary and training support of up to 90% through reskilling programmes such as career conversion programmes which support employers to upskill their new hires, including senior employees, to take on enhanced job roles such as in digital fields, where we know there are lots of exciting development.

sections.label: Employers holding career conversations
sections.summary: A ground-up approach is needed where employers hold regular structured career conversations with senior workers, as NTUC's Company Training Committees seek to do.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: A ground-up approach is thus needed where employers take ownership and conduct regular and structured career conversations with their senior workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: This is one of the key aspects that the NTUC's Company Training Committees (CTCs) seek to do – bringing together the employers, HR and employee representatives to identify gaps and opportunities and align the training plans for its workforce to its business transformation roadmap.

sections.label: Age-friendly workplace and fairness legislation
sections.summary: Employers are encouraged to approach TAFEP and adopt the Tripartite Standard on Age-friendly Workplace Practices, while a Tripartite Committee is looking into workplace fairness legislation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: I encourage employers to approach TAFEP to find out more.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: I would also like to encourage more employers to adopt the Tripartite Standard on Age-friendly Workplace Practices, which specifies a set of good age management practices and recognises progressive employers that implement them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: As announced last year, a Tripartite Committee is looking into enacting workplace fairness legislation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: This will broaden the range of measures and penalties available to address workplace discrimination, including age discrimination.
